title: Making and Using Compost
summary: Compost turns farm and kitchen waste into a free fertiliser that feeds crops, holds water and improves soil structure.
actions: Mix green material (fresh leaves, weeds, manure, kitchen scraps) with brown material (dry leaves, straw, maize stalks) at about 1:2
Build a heap at least 1 m wide and 1 m high, in the shade
Keep it as moist as a wrung-out cloth; cover with leaves or a sack
Turn the heap every 2 weeks; it is ready in 6–8 weeks when dark and crumbly
Apply 2–3 handfuls per planting hole or spread 2–5 cm over beds before planting

sections.heading: Ingredients
sections.body: Green material (fresh leaves, manure, kitchen scraps) plus brown material (dry leaves, straw). Avoid meat and diseased plants.

sections.heading: Method
sections.body: Layer green and brown, keep moist and turn every 2 weeks. Ready in 6–8 weeks when dark, crumbly and smelling of earth.

sections.heading: Using it
sections.body: Add 2–3 handfuls per planting hole, or spread over beds before planting. Use compost tea as a liquid feed.

title: Mulching
summary: A layer of dry grass, leaves or straw on the soil keeps moisture in, weeds down and protects leaves from soil splash.
actions: Spread 5–10 cm of dry grass, straw or leaves around plants after they are established
Keep mulch a few cm away from the stem to avoid rot
Top up as the mulch breaks down
In very wet weather pull mulch back slightly so the soil does not stay waterlogged

sections.heading: Why mulch
sections.body: Mulch cuts water loss by up to half, stops most weeds, keeps soil cool and prevents rain splashing disease onto lower leaves.

sections.heading: How
sections.body: Spread 5–10 cm of dry organic material around established plants, keeping it off the stems. Top up through the season.

title: Crop Rotation
summary: Changing the crop family in each bed every season breaks pest and disease cycles and balances soil nutrients.
actions: Follow a heavy feeder (maize, tomato) with a legume (beans, cowpea, peanut)
Never plant tomato, chili, potato or eggplant in the same bed two seasons in a row
Keep a simple record of what was planted where
A 3-year cycle is ideal: maize → beans → vegetables

sections.heading: The idea
sections.body: Pests and diseases build up when the same crop stays in the same soil. Rotating starves them and legumes add nitrogen for the next crop.

sections.heading: Simple plan
sections.body: Maize → beans → vegetables → maize. Keep tomato, chili and potato apart because they share diseases.

title: Protecting Sloping Land
summary: Much of Timor-Leste's farmland is on slopes; simple contour measures stop topsoil washing away in the wet season.
actions: Plant rows along the contour, not up and down the slope
Build contour lines of stones, vetiver grass or leucaena every 5–10 m of slope
Keep soil covered with mulch or a cover crop in the rains
Do not burn crop residue; leave it on the surface

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.body: Heavy rain on bare sloping soil removes the most fertile layer first. Yields drop year after year.

sections.heading: What to do
sections.body: Contour planting, grass strips or stone lines across the slope, and permanent soil cover.

title: Reading Your Soil
summary: Simple field tests tell you if soil is sandy, clay or loam and whether it drains well, guiding watering and compost use.
actions: Ribbon test: moisten soil and press between thumb and finger — no ribbon = sandy, long ribbon = clay, short ribbon = loam
Drainage test: dig a 30 cm hole, fill with water; if it takes over 4 hours to drain the soil is heavy
Sandy soil: add compost and mulch, water more often
Clay soil: add compost, raise beds, avoid working it wet
Ask your extension office about a pH test if crops grow poorly despite good care

sections.heading: Ribbon test
sections.body: Moist soil pressed between the fingers: sandy makes no ribbon, clay makes a long one, loam a short one.

sections.heading: What to do next
sections.body: Sandy: more compost and mulch. Clay: compost and raised beds. Poor growth despite care: ask about a pH test.
